patients.name: Harold Whitaker
problems: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, NYHA class III

encounters.summary: Guideline-directed medical therapy started for HFrEF
encounters.note: Dyspnea on walking one block, two-pillow orthopnea. Echocardiogram today: LVEF 30%. Started sacubitril/valsartan and carvedilol; spironolactone and dapagliflozin to be added at the two-week visit. Plan: titrate to target doses and reassess LVEF after at least three months of optimal therapy.

encounters.summary: Persistent NYHA class III symptoms after five months of optimal medical therapy
encounters.note: On target doses of sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, spironolactone and dapagliflozin since March 2026 (more than five months). Still breathless on minimal exertion, NYHA class III. Repeat echocardiogram: LVEF 28%. ECG: sinus rhythm, left bundle branch block, QRS duration 158 ms. Meets guideline criteria for cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillator: LVEF 35% or less, LBBB with QRS 150 ms or more, NYHA class III on optimal medical therapy for at least three months. Discussed with the patient; he consents. Referred for CRT-D implantation.

encounters.summary: CRT-D implantation, uncomplicated
encounters.note: Cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator implanted under local anesthesia and sedation. Right atrial, right ventricular and coronary sinus leads placed with good thresholds. No complications. Discharged the next day. Device check in two weeks.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for hypertension and diabetes.
encounters.note: Blood pressure 135/85 mm Hg, random glucose 210 mg/dL. Patient is taking metformin and lisinopril. Assessment: Poorly controlled hypertension and diabetes. Plan: Restart metformin and adjust lisinopril dose.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease.
encounters.note: Atrial fibrillation controlled with warfarin and metoprolol. Serum creatinine 2.1 mg/dL. Assessment: Controlled atrial fibrillation and stable kidney function. Plan: Monitor renal function and adjust medications as needed.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for hypothyroidism.
encounters.note: TSH 15.2 uU/mL. Patient taking levothyroxine. Assessment: Suboptimal thyroxine replacement. Plan: Increase levothyroxine dose.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for congestive heart failure.
encounters.note: Left ventricular ejection fraction 30%, serum B-type natriuretic peptide 400 pg/mL. Assessment: Poorly controlled congestive heart failure. Plan: Increase lisinopril and furosemide doses.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
encounters.note: Aortic systolic pressure 140 mm Hg, LDL 160 mg/dL. Patient taking lisinopril and atorvastatin. Assessment: Uncontrolled hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Plan: Adjust lisinopril and atorvastatin doses.

encounters.summary: Follow-up for atrial fibrillation and COPD.
encounters.note: Aortic systolic pressure 90 mm Hg, FEV1 2.5 L. Patient taking warfarin and albuterol. Assessment: Controlled atrial fibrillation and stable COPD. Plan: Monitor oxygen saturation and adjust medications as needed.

encounters.summary: Follow-up on chronic conditions.
encounters.note: BP 145/95 mmHg, Cholesterol 230 mg/dL. Continued to recommend lifestyle modifications with close follow-up. Also reviewed osteoarthritis management options.

encounters.summary: Reviewing current medication regimen and overall health.
encounters.note: Patient has worsening kidney function with decreased eGFR. Adjusted medications for heart failure and kidney disease. Recommended fluid restriction and monitoring.

encounters.summary: Review of Atrial Fibrillation and Osteoporosis.
encounters.note: Patient has persistent Atrial Fibrillation with no acute symptoms. Continued on anticoagulation therapy. Also, assessed for osteoporosis risk and started vitamin D supplements. Recommended follow-up in 3 months.

encounters.summary: Monitoring for chronic conditions.
encounters.note: BP 150/90 mmHg, eGFR 45 mL/min. Continued to recommend lifestyle modifications with close follow-up. Also, managed chronic kidney disease with medication adjustments.

encounters.summary: Follow-up on diabetes and cholesterol management.
encounters.note: Cholesterol 220 mg/dL, HbA1c 9%. Continued to stress the importance of diet and exercise for diabetes management. Also reviewed medication options for cholesterol management.

encounters.summary: Follow-up on Acute Coronary Syndrome.
encounters.note: Patient is asymptomatic with normal ECG. Continued on medication therapy for Acute Coronary Syndrome and High Cholesterol. Recommended close follow-up in 2 weeks for cardiac monitoring.

encounters.summary: Routine follow-up for atrial fibrillation management.
encounters.note: The patient's Atrial Fibrillation is well-controlled on current medication regimen. Blood pressure is elevated at 152/98 mmHg. Lipid profile is satisfactory. Continue current therapy and schedule follow-up in 6 weeks.

encounters.summary: Review of CAD, diabetes, and osteoporosis management.
encounters.note: The patient is in New York Heart Association Class II despite medical therapy. HbA1c is 7.5% with stable blood glucose levels. Continue statin therapy and schedule bone mineral density scan in 6 months.

encounters.summary: Management of congestive heart failure and COPD.
encounters.note: The patient's ejection fraction is 30% with stable dyspnea and edema. Pulmonary function test results show a slight decrease in FEV1. Continue current medication regimen and schedule follow-up in 3 months.

encounters.summary: Review of rheumatoid arthritis and hypertension management.
encounters.note: The patient's disease activity is well-controlled on current medication regimen. Blood pressure is elevated at 140/90 mmHg. Schedule follow-up in 6 weeks and refer to physical therapy for exercise program.

encounters.summary: Management of osteoarthritis and hyperlipidemia.
encounters.note: The patient reports improvement in joint pain with current medication regimen. Lipid profile shows elevated LDL levels. Continue current therapy and schedule follow-up in 3 months.

encounters.summary: Review of type 1 diabetes and allergy management.
encounters.note: The patient's HbA1c is 8.2% with stable blood glucose levels. Allergy testing shows a positive reaction to tree nuts. Schedule follow-up in 6 weeks and provide further education on diabetes management.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for CAD and diabetes.
encounters.note: The patient's blood pressure is well-controlled, and there are no signs of acute coronary syndrome. The cardiac medication regimen remains unchanged.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for CHF and HTN.
encounters.note: The patient's HF symptoms are stable. The ejection fraction remains low, but there are no signs of worsening heart failure. The diuretic regimen remains unchanged.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for HTN and angina.
encounters.note: The patient's blood pressure is elevated, but the patient is asymptomatic for angina. The hypertension medication regimen is adjusted to reduce the blood pressure.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for RA and osteoporosis.
encounters.note: The patient's rheumatoid arthritis symptoms are stable, and the joint inflammation is well-controlled. The osteoporosis medication regimen remains unchanged to prevent further bone loss.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for HTN and MI.
encounters.note: The patient's hypertension is well-controlled, but there are no signs of full recovery from the myocardial infarction. The cardiac medication regimen remains unchanged.

encounters.summary: Routine checkup for CHF and diabetes.
encounters.note: The patient's HF symptoms are stable, but the patient requires further medication adjustments to prevent further decompensation. The blood glucose levels remain well-controlled for the diabetes.
